messages.subject: Re: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory
messages.subject_clean: Using terraclimate with NCEP data on a local directory
messages.body_plain:
Hi Traci,

One more suggestion - make sure you're running complete years because I was just alerted to an issue with the terra climate code in NicheMapR that can come up if you don't. I.e., start on 01/01/year and end on 31/12/year. I'll sort that bug out soon (it's to do with ensuring rain falls at midnight under different time zones for the soil moisture calculations - if rain falls during the day the integrator can have trouble due to the sudden change in conditions).

All the best,
Mike

I think the error occurs on or after line 1052. All of the packages are recently downloaded and installed in haphazard order (because of the maintenance). Could this be two packages differing in how they deal with time?  I've tried running the code with only NicheMapR loaded. I really think this is a my HPC issue; when I first started running NicheMapR on it, I had to download packages in a certain order to get it to work.

messages.subject: Wind speed correction at ground level
messages.subject_clean: Wind speed correction at ground level
messages.body_plain:
Hello NicheMapR peeps,
I asked a question for Mike about the equation for correcting location windspeed by a reference windspeed, and he recommended posting the question here so that duplicate questions can be avoided. Here was my question and his answer:

Hi Mike,
What is the equation used to correct wind speed measured at a height to ground level?
For example, the wind speed was measured at a height of 10 m, but I want to correct it at ground level (2 cm height).

Hi Niky,
In general, if you have questions that aren’t very specific to a collaborative project, can you post your questions on the google group? That way others can learn too and I might avoid duplicating answers. But to answer your question, have a look through the NicheMapR help, specifically https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/microclimate-model-theory-equations – worth a general study of this and hopefully you’ll find most of your answers there. You can also see where this is done in micro_global (or any of the other functions):
https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/micro_global.R (from line 824)

# correct for fact that wind is measured at 10 m height
# wind shear equation v / vo = (h / ho)^a
#where
#v = the velocity at height h (m/s)
#vo = the velocity at height ho (m/s)
#a = the wind shear exponent
#Terrain Wind Shear Exponent
#- a -
# Open water 0.1
#Smooth, level, grass-covered 0.15 (or more commonly 1/7)
#Row crops 0.2
#Low bushes with a few trees 0.2
#Heavy trees 0.25
#Several buildings 0.25
#Hilly, mountainous terrain 0.25
# source http://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/wind-shear-d_1215.html

WNMINN <- WNMINN * (1.2 / 10) ^ 0.15
WNMAXX <- WNMAXX * (1.2 / 10) ^ 0.15

--

Nicholas C. Wu | PhD

Postdoctoral Research Fellow

Animal Ecology Lab | Hawkesbury Institute for the Environment

Western Sydney University, NSW 2753 | Australia

E: nichola...@gmail.com | M: +61 409 456 802 | W: http://wunicholas.wix.com/home

messages.subject: Installing NicheMapR on a Mac
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mac users,
If you've had trouble compilling NicheMapR, make sure you've got the right version of R for your chip (Intel vs am64 silicon) - R will still run if it's the wrong version but won't compile Fortran properly. Also, get the correct version of gfortran from here <https://mac.r-project.org/tools/>
All the best,
Mike
